standard_prerequisites.name: Numerical types, their recurrence conditions and their Picard group
standard_prerequisites.statement: A numerical type is a collection of integers n, m of subscript i, a of subscript i j, w of subscript i and g of subscript i whose intersection numbers are symmetric, whose diagonal entries are nonpositive with vanishing row sums weighted by the multiplicities, and whose weights divide the corresponding intersection numbers; its Picard group is the cokernel of the matrix of the divided intersection numbers. The chapter proves separately that under the recurrence conditions the intersection matrix has rank one less than its size, in two versions, one for real and one for symmetric data. The author's own definitions and those two lemmas are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma computes the rank of the Picard group of a numerical type, which the section needs when it compares Picard groups of types related by a contraction and when it identifies the Picard group in the case of nonpositive genus.

core_obligations: Single vertex: if the type has one vertex then the intersection matrix is the zero matrix, and the result is immediate because the Picard group is then free of rank one (source line 1135).

Several vertices: the intersection matrix has rank one less than its size, which the author reads off from the chapter's recurrence lemmas, one of which is stated for real data and the other for symmetric data (source lines 1136-1137).

Conclude the rank: scaling the rows by the inverses of the weights does not change the rank, so the cokernel of the divided intersection matrix, that is the Picard group, is finitely generated abelian of rank one (source lines 1138-1141).

proof_roadmap.step: The single-vertex case, where the matrix is zero and the group is free of rank one.
The rank of the intersection matrix from the chapter's recurrence lemmas.
Row scaling does not change the rank, so the cokernel has rank one.
